newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria plans to crack down on tax evasion.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria plans to crack down on tax evasion.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to impose a once-off 25 percent tax on all so far undeclared property in a bid to boost tax revenue, the president's economy adviser Krassimir Angarski said on Wednesday.
"I plan to propose to the new government and parliament to levy a once-off tax of 25 percent on all undeclared property from the past six to seven years," Angarski told a news conference.

Bulgaria will be unable to sustain a restrictive monetary regime, pledged to international lenders, without increasing tax collection. Around 50 percent of Bulgarians currently do not pay taxes on all their property and income, said Angarski.
"For those who fail to declare their proerty within a previously set term, the penalty would envisage confiscation and imprisonment," said Angarski.
The proposal is expected to be enforced next year after approval by the new government and parliament to be formed after early general elections on Apirl 19, he said.

Fines envisaged in current anti-tax evasion laws have melted to insignificant amounts after the dramatic slump of the national currency. The fines were calculated at around 70 levs per dollar exchange rate of 70. The lev now trades at around 1,600 per dollar.
"I plan to propose to the new government and parliament to set up a tax police with an information network which will monitor all new household acquisitions like cars and houses," said Angarski.

Under a $510 million 14-month standby accord signed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) last month, Bulgaria pledged to introduce a fixed exchange regime which curbs financial powers of the government and the central bank and prevents the printing of money. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
